Currently
column2: no lock or mutex is held between allocating a hugepage and

column1: inserting it into the pagetables / page cache.  When we do go to insert the
page into pagetables or page cache
column2: we recheck and may free the newly

column1: allocated hugepage.  However
column2: since the number of hugepages in the system

column1: is strictly limited
column2: and it's usualy to want to use all of them

column1: still lead to spurious allocation failures.
For example
column2: suppose two processes are both mapping (MAP_SHARED) the same

column1: hugepage file
column2: large enough to consume the entire available hugepage pool.

column1: If they race instantiating the last page in the mapping
attempt to allocate the last available hugepage.  One will fail
returning OOM from the fault and thus causing the process to be killed
despite the fact that the entire mapping can
The patch fixes this race by the simple method of adding a (sleeping) mutex
to serialize the hugepage fault path between allocation and insertion into
pagetables and/or page cache.  It would be possible to avoid the
serialization by catching the allocation failures
condition
column2: then rechecking to see if someone else has instantiated the page

column1: for us.  Given the likely frequency of hugepage instantiations
very doubtful it's worth the extra complexity.
This patch causes no regression on the libhugetlbfs testsuite
test
column2: which can trigger this race now passes where it previously failed.
